title: The teacher's charge to the student: "speak the truth, practice dharma" (1.11)
hook: one of the oldest graduation speeches in the world, and its most surprising line: copy our good deeds, not the others
tomorrow: "honor your mother as god, your father as god, your teacher, your guest"

segments.voice: Yesterday: purna. That is full, this is full, and the Brihadaranyaka closed. Your line was full from full.

Caps, gowns, a stage, and someone at a podium telling a room full of graduates how to live. Graduation speeches are mostly forgotten by dinner. Here's one that's lasted well over two thousand years. It's in a new Upanishad, the Taittiriya. A teacher has finished teaching the Veda to his student, years of it, line by line. The student is about to leave and start a life. Before he goes, the teacher stands up and gives him his charge.
screen: `CAPS, GOWNS, A PODIUM.` → `A NEW UPANISHAD.` → `THE TEACHER STANDS UP.`

segments.voice: First, the book. The Taittiriya belongs to the Black Yajurveda. A later legend explains its odd name, tittiri, partridges: when Yajnavalkya, our friend from the Brihadaranyaka, quarreled with his teacher and gave back what he'd learned, his fellow students took the form of partridges and gathered it up. Now the speech. It opens with three short commands that many Hindus know by heart: satyam vada, dharmam chara. Speak the truth. Practice dharma. And don't neglect your study. Then the practical part. Bring your teacher the gift he'd value. Don't let your family line be cut off. Don't drift from the truth, from dharma, from what keeps you well, from your own flourishing, from learning and teaching. And then a line you might not expect from a teacher. Whatever deeds of ours are blameless, those you should follow, not the others. Whatever good conduct is ours, honor that, not the rest. The teacher is admitting, at the graduation, that he isn't perfect. And one more, for every hard moment after graduation. If you're ever in doubt about what to do, he says, look at the people there who are wise, devoted, and gentle, and do as they would do. Then the teacher seals it. This is the command. This is the teaching. This is the secret of the Veda. After all those years, the secret is plain: tell the truth, do what's right, keep learning, and copy the best of the people who taught you.
screen: `THE TAITTIRIYA: THE PARTRIDGES' BOOK.` · `SPEAK THE TRUTH. PRACTICE DHARMA.` · `FOLLOW OUR GOOD DEEDS, NOT THE OTHERS.` · `IN DOUBT? LOOK AT THE WISE AND GENTLE.` · then, large: `THE GRADUATION SPEECH.`

segments.voice: Bring to mind someone who taught you something that mattered: a teacher, a parent, a coach, a grandparent. Let one of their good deeds come to mind, then, gently, one of their flaws, and hold both without judging. Then let the flaw go, and keep the good deed.
Satyam vada, speak the truth. The first words of the teacher's charge, as the student leaves to start a life.
Your line: the graduation speech. Tomorrow, the next part of the same speech. Day three hundred eighty-nine, done.

howItsDone: The teacher's charge in Taittiriya 1.11 is recited in traditional Vedic schools at the end of study, and satyam vada, dharmam chara is widely quoted in Indian schools and at graduation ceremonies.

chat.says: What did the teacher in the Taittiriya tell his student before he left?
options: Speak the truth, practice dharma, keep studying, and follow only his good deeds.
Never leave home, and spend the rest of your life studying the Veda.
Forget your studies now, since life is the only teacher you need.
chat.meaning: Satyam vada, dharmam chara: speak the truth, practice dharma. Then the teacher adds: follow our blameless deeds, not the others.

Taittiriya.meaning: the Upanishad of the Black Yajurveda this path is now reading

Yajurveda.meaning: one of the four Vedas; the Taittiriya belongs to its Black branch

tittiri.meaning: partridge; a later legend ties the book's name to it

dharmam chara.meaning: practice dharma, do what is right

sources.ref: Vishnu Purana 3.5 (the partridge legend of the Taittiriya branch)

notes: The index word is the title's head cut mid-word ("The teacher's charge to the student"); kept exactly. The word screen shows satyam vada.

The partridge (tittiri) legend: Yajnavalkya disgorged the Yajurveda after a quarrel with his teacher Vaishampayana, and the other students as partridges took it up (Vishnu Purana 3.5). Cited from memory; please confirm. The script says 'gave back what he'd learned'.

The charge's list (1.11.1) and 'follow our blameless deeds, not others' (1.11.2) and the doubt clause (1.11.4) are paraphrased. The mother/father/teacher/guest lines and the giving lines are held for day 390.
Use of satyam vada dharmam chara at Indian graduations/convocations: stated generally; confirm.
